primitives.name: Adaptability Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: Versatility[1], developed by John Hollinger and defined in equation (1) below, measures the ability for a player to score, rebound, and assist all the time, but not selectively choose when to score, rebound, and assist at any time given the personnel around them.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_i': 'Scoring propensity at time i, dimensionless', 'R_i': 'Rebounding rate at time i, dimensionless', 'A_i': 'Assisting frequency at time i, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Player performance components are independent and multiplicative across time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P_i, R_i, A_i approach zero, adaptability index vanishes.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Bayesian adaptability posterior over lineup permutations; GSE encodes this as a kernel-weighted entropy reduction in playstyle states.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between lineup composition and observed playstyle variance.

primitives.name: Portability Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Portability hasn't been rigorously defined by many however, craftedNBA[2] does have their own definition which is a weighted average of portable skills like low usage rates, high true shooting percentage, and high assisting.
primitives.latex: PM = w_1 \cdot U^{-1} + w_2 \cdot TS + w_3 \cdot A
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'PM': 'Portability measure, dimensionless', 'U': 'Usage rate, fraction', 'TS': 'True shooting percentage, fraction', 'A': 'Assists per game, dimensionless', 'w_1, w_2, w_3': 'Weight coefficients, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Portable skills are additive and linearly weighted in performance consistency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When U → 1, PM approaches negative infinity; when TS, A → 0, PM → -∞.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's conditional adaptability likelihood; GSE uses PM to compute robustness of state transitions in team dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Change in team efficiency under substitution of player X with Y.

primitives.name: Mutual Information Adaptability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Another interpretation is that portability is a measure of how easy it is for other players to adapt to the new player.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I(X;Y)': 'Mutual information, bits', 'f(x,y)': 'Joint probability density of lineup X and playstyle Y', 'f(x)': 'Marginal probability of lineup X', 'f(y)': 'Marginal probability of playstyle Y'}
primitives.assumptions: Lineup and playstyle are modeled as continuous random variables with joint distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When X and Y are independent, I(X;Y) = 0; when fully dependent, I(X;Y) → ∞.

layer2.mapping: Encodes GSI's adaptive likelihood kernel; GSE computes state transition entropy based on mutual information.
layer2.telemetry: Entropy reduction in playstyle upon observing lineup configuration.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Adaptability Index is derived from a product of three performance indicators—scoring, rebounding, and assisting—normalized by a cubic root to maintain dimensional consistency. It assumes that a player’s versatility is captured by the simultaneous presence of these traits across time. Portability, conversely, is a weighted sum of low usage, high true shooting, and assistive behavior, suggesting a player's utility across varying lineups. Mutual Information captures the dependency between lineup and playstyle, using continuous entropy to model nonlinear adaptability. These primitives are unified under an information-theoretic lens where adaptability is quantified as the capacity of a player to alter team dynamics through strategic flexibility. Failure modes include overfitting to static metrics, ignoring contextual dependencies, and assuming independence among performance dimensions. The framework avoids linear correlation methods due to discrete nature of lineup data and nonlinearity of playstyle evolution.
